name: Bell Labs travelling-wave erbium-doped fibre amplifier
summary: A laboratory fibre amplifier that directly boosted a near-infrared optical signal using erbium-doped single-mode fibre.
description: Bell Labs researchers Emmanuel Desurvire, Jay Simpson and Philip Becker reported 22 dB of gain in a 1.53 μm signal at room temperature in an erbium-doped single-mode fibre. The experiment was a laboratory demonstration.

date.label: by 1987-11-01
date.basis: Date of publication describing the already-performed demonstration.

events.statement: Bell Labs reported travelling-wave amplification of a 1.53 μm optical signal in erbium-doped fibre.
events.place_note: Bell Labs researchers based in New Jersey
events.caveats: A distinct Southampton team also reported an erbium-doped fibre amplifier in 1987. This event makes no global priority claim.

evidence.locator: Optics Letters 12(11), pp. 888–890, author affiliations, History and abstract
evidence.supports: The original abstract states the gain, operating wavelength, fibre type and room-temperature condition.

caveats: The Southampton team’s contemporaneous achievement is separately documented by Mears and colleagues. The Bell Labs report concerns laboratory performance.

research.note: Proposed for independent admission review. Researcher gpt-6.2-sol, high.
